matches.quote: "Dynamic skyrmion velocity" is not defined (peak or pulse average)... The authors should... define J and v... and discuss the mobility relative to ref. 21.
STXM projects through 25 repeats, and hybrid or non-uniform skyrmion tubes have been reported in related SyAFMs (ref. 39)... comment on whether depth-dependent dynamics could be hidden
Sublattice A is FCB(0.4)/CFB(0.2) (Fig. 1a) and contains Co, so the Co-edge XMCD signal is the Co moment of B minus that of A
The statement that "an AFM skyrmion lattice has, to our knowledge, not yet been experimentally realized" (p. 2) should be reconciled with refs. 19–22 and 38
If local wells exert restoring forces on L and R skyrmions, the fit folds those forces into a* and b*, which undermines the headline claim
A control in which the scattering partner is absent (an isolated skyrmion or a sparse region under identical pulses) would separate interaction-driven recoil from pinning-well relaxation

Without a model comparison, "reveals an exponential decay" is an assumption rather than a result... compare losses for alternative forms (the modified-Bessel K1(r/λ) form expected from exchange-mediated texture overlap
"Tracking the voltage" compares against the applied voltage, not the current in the strip... fit the displacement or v(t) against the drive... measure the transmitted current waveform
The class thresholds on net displacement (Fig. 2a) are not given... The authors should give... the number of skyrmions per class... the class criteria and the sensitivity to them
"defying theoretical predictions" (p. 13) needs the delay and separation that ref. 43 predicts for this stack's interlayer coupling (using the 650 mT spin-flop and 1.8 T saturation fields
The velocity of about 50 m/s... is far below SyAFM velocities in ref. 21, which bears on... whether the regime is viscous or creep-like.
Transient Joule heating is not characterised... estimate the peak temperature rise during and after each pulse at both current densities, from the device resistance... or from a thermal model
Relaxation times for the same class differ by up to a factor of five between polarities... which a symmetric bipolar drive acting on a pairwise potential does not obviously produce
It does not say whether... a* and b* recur in another device, another region... or after re-nucleating the lattice... show at least one independent repeat of the inversion

notes: C2 and C7 are marked partly: P12 and P24 question whether the high-drive regime is viscous vs creep-like, ask for threshold fits and regime labelling on v(J), and propose an isolated-skyrmion control, without framing the issue explicitly as single-skyrmion vs crystal regime equivalence. C10 is marked partly via P6 and P17, which address projection and rigid-locking assumptions across the 25 multilayer repeats. C16 is marked partly via P13 and P26, which question the rigid-particle pairwise Thiele assumption under asymmetric deformation and whether the fitted potential is invariant across lattice configurations.
